title: 6. 10-Year Financial Forensics, Cash Conversion & Balance Sheet

epigraph.quote: Cash flow is a fact; GAAP net income in an acquisitive biopharma is an accounting opinion shaped by expensed IPR&D and intangible write-downs.
epigraph.author: Forensic Accounting Desk

web_blocks.html: A quick look at Gilead's 2026 stock screens shows alarming negative GAAP numbers. Trailing-twelve-month (TTM) net income is -$3.86 billion, ROE is -22.34%, and ROIC is -10.48% [18]. A closer look at 10-year filings and 2026 Form 10-Q reports explains why. Those GAAP losses stem from M&A accounting rules rather than weak operations, though past deals did leave real capital scars [1, 18]. Across all ten years from 2016 to 2025, operating cash flow never fell below $8.0 billion a year [1].

Under U.S. GAAP (ASC 730 / ASC 805), buying a clinical-stage company for an unapproved drug counts as an asset purchase, not a business merger. That rule forces the buyer to expense the purchase price right away as Acquired IPR&D on the income statement. That exact rule hit Gilead twice in three years. In FY2024, $4.3B for CymaBay plus a $2.4B Trodelvy write-down cut GAAP net income to $480M, even though operating cash flow hit $10.83B [11, 19]. In Q2 2026, closing the $7.8 billion Arcellx buyout plus Tubulis and Ouro deals pushed 2026E acquired IPR&D to ~$12.4 billion. That charge caused a Q2 2026 GAAP loss of $(8.45) per share [18].

web_blocks.takeaway: Across 10 years, Gilead's Operating Cash Flow never fell below $8.0B/yr and averaged ~$10.4B/yr, proving the underlying HIV franchise's cash durability even when GAAP net income was depressed by M&A accounting.

web_blocks.html: Cash Conversion, Balance Sheet & Leverage Post-CymaBay and Arcellx: In FY2025, Gilead generated $10,019 million in operating cash flow and spent $563 million on CapEx. That left $9,456 million in free cash flow, a 32.1% FCF margin and 111% of GAAP net income ($8,510 million) [1]. Out of that cash, Gilead paid ~$4.0 billion in dividends ($3.25/share TTM, growing ~2.7%–3.0% a year) and bought back ~$1.9 billion in stock. The remaining ~$3.5 billion of excess FCF went toward debt and bolt-on deals [1, 3].

On the balance sheet, Gilead's liquidity tightened materially during 2026 as M&A closed. From $10.6 billion in cash and marketable securities at year-end 2025, Gilead liquidated all $3,042 million of its marketable debt securities and ended Q3 2026 (September 30, 2026) with $6,437 million ($6.4 billion) in cash against $26,231 million ($26.2 billion) of total debt ($2,416 million current + $23,815 million long-term) [4]. Net debt rose to $19,794 million (~$19.8 billion, ~1.55x FY2025 EBITDA). Meanwhile, $11,307 million of 9M 2026 acquired IPR&D charges plus a $1,750 million ($1.75 billion) Q2 2026 IPR&D impairment on Trodelvy in NSCLC (wiping indefinite-lived IPR&D from $2.3 billion to $0) shrank stockholders' equity by 42.6%—from $22,703 million to $13,040 million (2.01x Debt/Equity). Footnote forensics also highlight $21,738 million of combined Goodwill ($8,314M) and Net Intangibles ($13,424M)—42.3% of total assets ($51,408M)—alongside $4,624 million in accrued rebates and a $1.1 billion liability related to future royalties from the 2020 Immunomedics acquisition.

web_blocks.title: Forensic Watchlist: Dividend Coverage vs. De-Leveraging
paragraphs: Gilead's ~$4.0B annual dividend uses ~42% of FY2025 FCF ($9.46B) and is well covered by steady HIV cash flows. After the $7.8B cash outlay for Arcellx and the $32B U.S. CapEx plan, share buybacks will likely take a back seat. Rebuilding cash and paying down debt ahead of the 2028 Biktarvy IRA reset should come first.

book_paragraphs: If you pull up a quantitative screener on Gilead Sciences in late 2026, the first three numbers that jump off the page look alarming: trailing twelve-month GAAP net income of negative $3.86 billion, return on equity of negative 22.3%, and return on invested capital of negative 10.5%. An investor who stops there would assume Gilead is losing money. You and I know better—because we are going to look under the hood of pharmaceutical accounting.

Why is GAAP net income negative in 2026 when Q3 2026 base business sales just grew 16% and Non-GAAP EPS was $2.55? The answer lies in U.S. GAAP asset-acquisition rules. When Gilead closed its $7.8 billion acquisition of Arcellx in April 2026—alongside deals with Tubulis and Ouro Medicines—accounting rules required Gilead to expense nearly the entire purchase price immediately on the income statement as Acquired In-Process Research and Development. That pushed 2026 acquired IPR&D charges to roughly $12.4 billion, swinging Q2 2026 into a massive GAAP accounting loss even though the underlying cash-generating engine didn't miss a beat.

To see the real economic truth, look at Gilead's 10-year cash flow statement from 2016 through 2025. Even as Hepatitis C fell from its 2015 peak, even through the 2020 deal spree, even as Veklury faded, Gilead's operating cash flow never once dipped below $8.0 billion in a single year—averaging $10.4 billion annually across a full decade. In FY2025, a clean year without mega-deal charges, Gilead turned $29.44 billion of revenue into $10.02 billion of operating cash flow and $9.46 billion of free cash flow.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: Do not let GAAP asset-acquisition rules fool you into thinking Gilead is unprofitable—and do not let Non-GAAP adjustments fool you into forgetting that $49 billion of cumulative M&A cash actually left the building. Both truths matter.

book_subsections.title: Balance Sheet, Leverage, and the Dividend
paragraphs: Look at how Gilead allocates that $9.46 billion of annual free cash flow. Roughly $4.0 billion goes straight to the dividend, which has grown steadily at roughly 3% a year and consumes just 42% of free cash flow. Another $1.9 billion in 2025 went to share repurchases. That left more than $3.5 billion of surplus cash before M&A.

On the balance sheet, liquidity tightened noticeably during 2026 after $11.3 billion of year-to-date acquisition cash outflows. Gilead sold off all $3.04 billion of its marketable debt securities and exited September 30, 2026 with $6.44 billion in cash against $26.23 billion of total debt—lifting net debt to $19.79 billion, or roughly 1.55x FY2025 EBITDA. At the same time, $11.31 billion of 9M 2026 acquired IPR&D charges and a $1.75 billion Q2 2026 write-down on Trodelvy in non-small cell lung cancer cut stockholders' equity by 42.6% to $13.04 billion. Meanwhile, $21.74 billion of goodwill and intangibles (42% of total assets), $4.62 billion of accrued rebates, and a $1.1 billion Immunomedics royalty liability sit on the balance sheet—making cash rebuild and debt paydown ahead of the 2028 Biktarvy IRA reset a top priority.
